note: Re-judged 2026-10-24 (independent auditor, authored none of the change). RFC 4760 Section 3: "If the Next Hop is allowed to be from more than one Network Layer protocol, the encoding of the Next Hop MUST provide a way to determine its Network Layer protocol." 238bdb62e9 (spec-refuse-instead-of-defaulting) changed nlri.NewINET to take an explicit has-path-id flag; the unit passes false where it passed path id 0, which already meant no ADD-PATH identifier, so the input, the route and every assertion are byte-for-byte the same (TestBuildRIBRouteUpdate_RefusesANextHopWithNoWireForm). The refusal of a next hop with no wire form and its accepting cases are unchanged. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgement follows. The one multi-protocol case Ze encodes is IPv4 NLRI over an IPv4 or an IPv6 next hop (RFC 5549/8950), plus RD-prefixed VPN hops. (a) forbidden: an encoding whose Length of Next Hop does not tell which protocol the hop is, e.g. an IPv6 hop under AFI 1 written with length 4, or a zero-length field. (b) TestMPReachNextHopLengthCountsTheOctetsWritten asserts buf[3]==16 for "ipv4 unicast over an ipv6 next hop" and 4 for the IPv4 hop, and that the written span equals Len(); negatives: TestMPReachValidateNextHopsRefusesAnAddressWithNoWireForm (ErrUnencodableNextHop, nothing written), TestCommitRefusesAnAnnounceWhoseNextHopHasNoWireForm and TestBuildRIBRouteUpdate_RefusesANextHopWithNoWireForm (no UPDATE on the commit and RIB-replay rails), TestParseMPReachNLRI_InvalidNextHopLength (length 5 refused). Tag-prose note: TestParseMPReachNLRI claims the parser derives the family from the length, but its cases are AFI 2 only and assert counts, not the family.
